content:
If I add the attribute to_fun to the lemma

theorem integrable_neg_iff {f : α → β} : Integrable (-f) μ ↔ Integrable f μ := ...

it works fine, and creates a lemma saying that Integrable (fun i ↦ -f i) μ ↔ Integrable f μ, which is exactly what I want. Except that it gives to it the name fun_integrable_neg_iff instead of the one I'd like, i.e., integrable_fun_neg_iff. Is there a way to prescribe a lemma name by hand?

Also, if I just put @[to_fun] before the lemma, then hovering over it gives me the name of the new lemma. But I don't know how to go to the definition of to_fun or to get its docstring. But if I put @[to_fun (attr := simp)] and hover, I get a docstring for to_fun but I don't get the new lemma name (and still no way to go to the definition of to_fun). Am I missing some tricks here?
I have the same problem with naming (and created #34257 to fix this). It's waiting on me to incorporate Jovan's review comments. I will get to that eventually, but probably only in a few weeks.

The hover information is tricky. I think seeing the new lemma is better than only seeing the documentation of to_fun; I'm not sure if there's a way to have both. (This is the same to to_additive.) For @[to_fun mylemmaname], we could have to_fun show the attribute doc-string and mylemmaname the generated statement.

Yes, it's not possible to have both

  • hover info of the generated lemma
  • doc-string and go-to-def of to_fun

I'm very surprised that the lemma hover doesn't work in combination with (attr := ...). I've made a fix/improvement at #36894 now.

Michael Rothgang said:

For @[to_fun mylemmaname], we could have to_fun show the attribute doc-string and mylemmaname the generated statement.

to_additive/to_dual already do this: it shows the generated lemma over the lemma name if there is a user-specified name, and otherwise over the to_additive keyword.
